text:
jordan: Bringing up kohlrabi (multilang embed, Mistral-derived) — quick smoke showed a weird language-specific drop after int4 quant. EN/FR fine, JA drops hard. Anyone seen a collapse like this only for one language?
michelle: Can you paste the numbers?
jordan: Baseline fp16 recall@1/5/10 -> en 0.84/0.93/0.96, fr 0.78/0.90/0.94, ja 0.72/0.86/0.91
jordan: int4 (calib=default english+fr) recall@1/5/10 -> en 0.82/0.92/0.95, fr 0.75/0.88/0.93, ja 0.50/0.73/0.86 :frowning:
sam: Oof. First suspects: normalization timing or calibration distribution. If calib was english-heavy the dynamic ranges for ja tokens might be off. Also: are we doing per-tensor or per-channel quant?
jordan: I used our standard int4 symmetric per-tensor pipeline for speed. Normalization is applied at serving time (post-embedding). There was a recent change to do a final L2-normalize in the model export step for int4 only — not for fp16. Could be related.
elaine: Also check tokenizer differences — if the new model changed tokenization for ja (subword merges) average embedding norms could shift.
jordan: here's the eval command I ran:
```
python eval_embeddings.py --model kohlrabi:int4 --dataset langmix_holdout --metrics recall@1,5,10 --batch-size 32 --normalize True
```
And raw recall CSV snippet I dumped:
```
model,lang,recall@1,recall@5
kohlrabi-fp16,en,0.84,0.93
kohlrabi-fp16,fr,0.78,0.90
kohlrabi-fp16,ja,0.72,0.86
kohlrabi-int4,en,0.82,0.92
kohlrabi-int4,fr,0.75,0.88
kohlrabi-int4,ja,0.50,0.73
```
michelle: That int4 ja drop is huge for recall@1. Can you run the eval with normalization toggled off to see raw cos similarity distribution? Might reveal scaling collapse.
sam: Quick local snippet you can run to compare normalized vs raw sims:
```python
import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity
E = np.load('embeddings_ja.npy')
raw = cosine_similarity(E_query, E_corpus)
norm = cosine_similarity(E_query / np.linalg.norm(E_query, axis=1, keepdims=True), E_corpus / np.linalg.norm(E_corpus, axis=1, keepdims=True))
print(raw.mean(), norm.mean())
```
sam: If raw sims are also low then model drift; if raw high but norm low then numeric underflow/zeroing during quant+norm path.
jordan: ran that quick test — raw mean sim for ja on int4 is ~0.12 vs fp16 raw ~0.36. So it's not only a normalization bug, something is shrinking vector magnitudes after quant.
elaine: Could be a scale-clipping issue during calibration: int4 symmetric quant with outlier clipping could be clipping high-variance dims used by ja. Did you use a multilingual calibration set?
jordan: No — calib was the small perf-oriented set (english heavy). I will re-run calibration including ja and per-channel quant.
michelle: Good. Also check if embedding dim order changed in the export (we had a bug before where dims were transposed when switching attention heads -> effective axis mismatch). If dims got permuted you could get low similarity in specific languages.
jordan: I inspected the saved npy shapes: (N,768) consistent. But I'll diff a few vectors between fp16 and int4 to see whether element-wise clipping happens.
ops: @jordan noted — hold the canary for kohlrabi-int4 until we verify multilingual stability?
deploy-bot: Reminder: canary rollout for kohlrabi-int4 scheduled at 23:00 UTC.
jordan: A quick follow-up after 38m: ran three checks — (A) per-channel int4 quant, (B) recalib with langmix (en+fr+ja), (C) disable post-export L2-normalize. Results:
```
A) per-channel int4 + old calib -> ja recall@1 = 0.64 (big improvement)
B) per-channel int4 + langmix calib -> ja recall@1 = 0.70 (nearly FP16 0.72)
C) disable post-export normalize -> tiny diff vs B; normalization not main cause
```
jordan: So per-channel quant + balanced calibration fixed most of it. Likely calibration bias clipped key dims used by ja.
sam: Nice! That points to recommending per-channel quant for multilingual models and/or ensuring calibration lang coverage. Can you open a quant-recs PR to make per-channel default for multilang models?
jordan: Yep opening PR now with benchmark artifacts and calibration script. Link: https://git.redwood/kohlrabi/quant-recs/pull/42 :thumbsup:
michelle: Great. Block the canary until perf test completes and add a quick lang-coverage check to the quant pipeline. :eyes:
elaine: Also add a tiny unit test that runs a few ja queries through calibration step to prevent regressions.
jordan: Will add tests + update docs. Thanks all — saved the rollout.
